reason: The text presents Job as a righteous, pious leader whose household functions harmoniously. His servants perform their duties managing his vast livestock without indication of discord, and his children engage in normal social activities (feasting together) without any sign of antagonism toward their father. The calamities described (Sabeans stealing cattle, divine fire consuming sheep, Chaldeans raiding camels, wind killing the children) are external disasters and divine tests—not evidence of internal conflict or antagonism from Job's people toward his leadership. Job maintains his authority and faith throughout, responding with dignified acceptance rather than dealing with any popular opposition.
